rows.description:
The Club at Eaglebrooke, located in Lakeland, FL , is pleased to announce an excellent career opportunity for a full-time Line Cook ! We are seeking a driven individual who is eager to learn, contribute, and grow within a fast‑paced hospitality-focused property organization. As part of Troon , you'll contribute to a global leader in golf and community management.

The Line Cook will assist the Chef/Kitchen Manager in preparing food for all food outlets on the property. The Line Cook will also perform other related tasks to food preparation and kitchen sanitation/cleanliness as directed by the Chef/Kitchen Manager. This position requires adhering to all procedural guidelines established by the Food Service and Safety Department.

1-2 years of cooking experience preferred.
Minimum education: High School (or equivalent) Diploma.
Experience in managing and upholding a safe working condition.
Understanding the knowledge of safety, sanitation and food handling procedures.
Must be dependable.
Must be able to work well in a fast-paced environment.

rows.title: Software Engineer
rows.description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Stripe Terminal helps businesses extend their online presence into the physical world by making it easy to accept in-person payments.
The Logistics Engineering team builds the systems and web experiences that support the end-to-end lifecycle of Stripe Terminal devices - from manufacturing and inventory to ordering, fulfillment, returns, warranties, and repairs. We develop web interfaces, infrastructure, APIs, integrations, and internal tools that connect Stripe with manufacturers, logistics providers, repair centers, and Terminal users around the world.
Our mission is to make complex physical-device operations simple and scalable. We build secure, reliable systems that help users manage orders and devices while supporting Stripe’s day-to-day logistics operations.
What you’ll do:
Responsibilities
Scope, design, build, and maintain large-scale systems that support the end-to-end lifecycle of Stripe Terminal devices, including ordering, fulfillment, returns, warranties, and repairs.
Develop APIs, integrations, and internal tools that connect Stripe with manufacturers, logistics providers, repair centers, and other partners.
Build intuitive web experiences that help Terminal users and internal teams order devices, manage orders, and handle returns and repairs.
Improve the efficiency and scalability of logistics operations by identifying patterns and simplifying complex workflows.
Debug and resolve critical production issues across services and multiple levels of the stack.
Collaborate with engineers, product managers, designers, operations teams, and other stakeholders to bring new capabilities to Terminal users.
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Requirements
A strong technical background, including 2-5 years of professional software development experience
Familiarity with the full life cycle of software development, from design and implementation to testing and deployment.
Empathy, strong communication skills and effective communication with stakeholders
A learning mindset, regardless of level or experience
The ability to drive clear next steps when encountering ambiguous spaces without clear lines of ownership
High standards for code quality and a constructive attitude to help others raise the bar
An ability to think creatively and holistically about reducing risk in a complex environment

rows.title: Pharmacy Technician
rows.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Job Purpose and Summary: 
At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work.  We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day and our Pharmacy Technicians (Technicians) play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise.
As a Technician, you will support the pharmacy team in delivering operational and service excellence within your store. Technicians are often the first point of contact to assist our patients and customers to deliver an exceptional experience. Technicians assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. Technicians operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout their shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, they demonstrate genuine care and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.
Once in role, Technicians are required to complete a rigorous company training program and satisfy all registration, licensing, and certification requirements according to their State’s Board of Pharmacy guidelines. Until the Pharmacy Technician has completed all necessary requirements, duties may be restricted by the Pharmacy Manager. 
A Technician is responsible for contributing to safe and effective operations of the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

About you and this role   
Dow has an exciting opportunity for a Paralegal in Midland, MI .  In this role, you will provide operational support to paralegals, attorneys, and other legal professionals in Dow Legal, with primary support for Innovation Law docketing activities, as a member of the Core Legal Practices – Technology & Operations team. 
You will provide critical technology, systems, and operations support to Core Legal Practices and Commercial & Innovation Law, including but not limited to, patent, trademark, copyright, and related intellectual property processes. You will support accurate legal operations data, efficient case administration, formal documentation, patent docketing and filing activities, and collaboration with internal teams, external vendors, counsel, agents, and records contacts. Success in this role requires strong attention to detail, sound judgment, initiative, systems proficiency, and the ability to support process consistency, team continuity, and operational effectiveness across Legal and the broader Company. 
General responsibilities 
Maintain a clear understanding of role responsibilities, including scope, boundaries, and appropriate escalation points. 
Complete assignments with initiative, attention to detail, and sound discretion under moderate supervision. 
Exercise logical judgment by recognizing when guidance, coordination, or escalation is needed. 
Contribute as an engaged member of the team by delivering legal support services within established parameters, procedures, and oversight. 
Participate in knowledge transfer, cross-training, and shared learning activities by sharing knowledge, experience, and best practices to strengthen team capability, effectiveness, continuity, and business resilience. 
Partner effectively with team members to balance workload, provide backup support, and share accountability for any joint/shared responsibilities. 
Maintain working knowledge of applicable Company policies, guidelines, and internal controls, including authorization, delegation of authority, agreement approval/signature guidelines, and third-party due diligence requirements, among others. 
Maintain proficiency in Legal, Company, and vendor systems used to support assigned responsibilities; engage subject matter experts, as needed, to ensure alignment with current best practices and recommended use. 
Apply creativity to solve problems or to develop/suggest new or improved processes and proactively identify and suggest changes which enhance the team's effectiveness and productivity.  
Specific Responsibilities 
Support U.S. and international patent docketing and filing operations by providing docketing services for patents and oppositions, maintaining IPMS patent law updates and related docketing impacts, processing new filing requests, and coordinating abandonment processing for patents not linked to contracts. 
Read and analyze all incoming client mail (including U.S. Mail, e-mail, courier packages, faxes) for the IP Case Team that relates to patent matters to determine due dates or reminder dates that need to be entered into the IPMS and annotates docketing entries as appropriate. 
Collaborate with internal teams, records center contacts, external vendors, and other third parties to support case administration; maintain work processes aligned with U.S. and international patent and trademark office requirements; manage incoming case mail and sold-patent correspondence; process country-specific working statements; and coordinate job folder, agreement, and patent retention/discard activities and projects. 
Maintain accurate operations data, system records, reference resources, and authority documentation by performing data integrity reviews, company name audits, Secretary’s file maintenance, firm/agent and Dow entity/subsidiary updates, delegation of authority table maintenance, U.S. and European applicant list reviews, and updates to Powers of Attorney. Investigate and perform research using external sources, as necessary.

rows.title: Director, Warehouse Operations & Production Supply
rows.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
The Global Material Movement team is responsible for every movement of material from a supplier's dock to the point of use on Anduril's production lines. We receive, inspect, store, count, kit and deliver the parts that build Anduril's products, and we hold custody of government property along the way. The team exists so that production never stops for material. As Anduril adds production lines and new buildings, warehouse capacity limits how fast each new product can ramp. Site Execution and Production Supply is the operating core of that team: the people, the floor and the daily results at Anduril's headquarters and Orange County facilities.
ABOUT THE JOB
We are looking for a Director, Warehousing Site Execution and Production Supply to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA. In this role, you will be responsible for warehouse and production supply operations across our headquarters and Orange County facilities: receiving, put away, picking, kitting, line side delivery and outbound shipping. You will lead a team of managers and supervisors and several hundred hourly associates, and you will open a new campus in Long Beach. Government property and export controlled material stay in custody the whole way. This will require experience running high volume, multi site warehouse operations by the numbers: labor planned against demand, productivity measured by process, and every miss traced to a root cause. If you are someone who walks the floor before you read the dashboard, can launch a building and get it to rate quickly, and builds supervisors who run their shifts through standard work and continuous improvement, then this role is for you.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Run daily operations across our headquarters and Orange County sites: receiving, put away, storage, picking, kitting, line side delivery, and outbound shipping to other Anduril sites and to deployment.
Own the result production cares about most: zero line stoppages caused by material, with dock to stock, kit on time and line side fill rate held to the service levels agreed with each production team. Every miss gets an A3 with a root cause, a countermeasure, an owner and a date.
Run the operation from data. Build the daily view of labor, productivity by process, backlog and service level by site, pulled from the system rather than from spreadsheets, and use it to staff every shift.
Lead from the floor through daily Gemba walks, tier meetings at every site, and a steady pace of kaizen events that each target a measured problem.
Own safety and cost at every site you run: zero recordables as the standard, the operating budget for labor, overtime, supplies and equipment, and cost per unit handled reported monthly to Finance.
Hold transaction discipline and location control in every flow you run, so the counts run by our Inventory Control and Quality Assurance team find nothing to fix. Execute quality at the point of handling: receiving checks, damage prevention and segregation of nonconforming material.
Keep government furnished property and export controlled material segregated, serialized and traceable in every flow you run.
Hire, train and develop hourly associates and the supervisors who lead them. Manage labor to the productivity standards and staffing guidelines set for each process, and manage overtime and attrition against plan.
Launch the Long Beach campus: hire its leaders, write its standard work, and run it to the same measures as headquarters from the first shift.
Act as the first user of every new system and layout. Test warehouse system changes on the floor before they go live, and accept or reject layout and automation handovers from Material Flow Engineering.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, industrial engineering, business or a related field, OR 15+ years of equivalent operations experience
12+ years of experience in fulfillment, distribution, 3PL or warehouse operations, including leadership of a high volume site
6+ years leading managers or supervisors across multiple shifts or sites, with 200+ hourly associates and full ownership of safety, labor and productivity results
Experience managing labor to engineered or measured productivity standards by process
Experience running warehouse operations on a warehouse management system
Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed to meet production milestones
Ability to travel up to 25% of the time
This position is based in Costa Mesa, CA and requires being onsite. Remote work not considered. Candidates outside the area must be willing to relocate to Costa Mesa, CA
U.S. Person status is required, as this position needs access to export controlled material and data
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Launched a new fulfillment, distribution or production supply site from pre opening through steady rate
Builds own analysis in SQL, Python or a BI tool
Experience supplying a manufacturing production line through kitting, kanban and line side replenishment
Aerospace, defense or regulated manufacturing experience, including custody of government furnished property
Led the operations side of a warehouse management system implementation or migration
Lean or Six Sigma certification, or a documented record of kaizen results
Supervisors you hired and developed were later promoted
Master's degree in supply chain, engineering or business
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance
US Salary Range
$220,000 — $292,000 USD 
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 
Benefits 
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications: 
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

rows.title: Cognitive Systems Lead
rows.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.
We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.
Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.
We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. The work on this transformation starts right now, with development inside our new 160,000 square foot Proto-Factory in Orange County, California, where the team is already laying the foundation. As the prototyping hub for Arsenal-2, this facility gives us a multi-year head start, proving out the advanced manufacturing methods, digital workflows, and quality systems that will scale across our broader shipyard network.
In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea—and this is the moment to join us.
ABOUT THE JOB
You will own the Cognitive subsystem for a maritime autonomous vehicle, owning navigation and control, the vehicle management system, communications, and protective systems. Reporting to the Vehicle Systems Lead, you will set architecture for how the vehicle navigates, communicates, manages itself, and protects itself across long-range autonomous operations.
Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own the Cognitive subsystem architecture: navigation and control, VMS, communications, and protective systems
Drive GN&C design including inertial navigation, safe navigation systems, and actuation control software
Drive Vehicle Management System design including route planning and casualty monitoring
Own communications architecture across BLOS, LOS, and acoustic domains
Define protective systems for vehicle survivability
Define interfaces between cognitive subsystem and body, energy, and mission systems
Manage subsystem schedule and cost performance across prototype, LRIP, and FRP phases
Provide technical mentorship to engineers across cognitive disciplines
Drive design-for-manufacturability in coordination with Production
Represent the cognitive subsystem in technical and customer meetings
Interface with Vehicle Systems Lead and Chief Engineer on technical decisions
Travel up to 25% to test sites and customer locations
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or equivalent
8+ years of experience in GN&C, vehicle autonomy, or embedded systems for marine, aerospace, or robotic platforms
Experience taking navigation, control, or communications systems through full product development cycles
Demonstrated experience with navigation systems, control systems, or communications architectures
Experience transitioning designs from prototype to production

AI Engineer 5 
At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to continuing to build world-class applied science and engineering teams to deliver our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build. 
Team Description: 
The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. We work hand-in-hand with our partners across the company to advance the state of the art in science and AI engineering, and we build and deploy proprietary solutions that are central to our business and deliver value to millions of customers.  Our AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products with the transformative power of AI, in responsible and scalable ways for the highest leverage impact. 
What You’ll Do:  
Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital One. 
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, agents and multi-agent workflows, similarity search, guardrails, model evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc. 
Leverage a broad stack of Open Source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, PyTorch, and more. 
Invent and introduce state-of-the-art foundation model optimization techniques to improve the performance — scalability, cost, latency, throughput — of large scale production AI systems. 
Contribute to the technical vision and the long term roadmap of foundational AI systems at Capital One. 
Design, implement and optimize multi-model orchestration pipelines - integrating LLMs, vector search, and domain-specific models into unified systems 
Establish and lead cost-performance governance reviews across AI systems, tracking GPU utilization, model throughput, and inference cost efficiency 
Lead team design councils or design review boards to ensure technical consistency and compliance with AI engineering standards 
Mentor Principal and Manager-level AI engineers, fostering cross-domain learning and elevating organizational technical maturity 
The Ideal Candidate:  
You love to build systems, take pride in the quality of your work, and also share our passion to do the right thing. You want to work on problems that will help change banking for good 
Passion for staying abreast of the latest research, and an ability to intuitively understand scientific publications and judiciously apply novel techniques in production 
You adapt quickly and thrive on bringing clarity to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and digging deep to uncover the root of problems and can articulate your findings concisely with clarity. You have the courage to share new ideas even when they are unproven 
You are deeply Technical. You possess a strong foundation in engineering and mathematics, and your expertise in hardware, software, and AI enables you to see and exploit optimization opportunities that others miss 
You are a resilient trailblazer who can forge new paths to achieve business goals when the route is unknown 
Basic Qualifications:  
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 6 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies, or a Master's degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 4 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies 
At least 6 years of experience programming with Python, Go, Scala, CUDA, or Java 
Preferred Qualifications:  
Experience leading development AI systems with tradeoff decisions around cost, latency, throughput and accuracy 
7+ years of experience deploying scalable and responsible AI solutions on cloud platforms (e.g. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or equivalent private cloud) 
Experience designing, developing, delivering, and supporting complex AI systems 
Experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies (e.g. LLM Inference, Similarity Search and VectorDBs, Guardrails, Memory) using Python, C++, C#, Java, CUDA, or Golang 
Experience developing and applying state-of-the-art techniques for optimizing training and inference software to improve hardware utilization, latency, throughput, and cost 
Experience in building agentic AI systems and agentic workflows 
Passion for staying abreast of the latest AI research and AI systems, and judiciously apply novel techniques in production 
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate complex AI concepts to peers 
Experience architecting and integrating heterogeneous AI systems - including rule-based, retrieval-augmented, and generative components - into unified production pipelines 
Experience defining and enforcing standards for ethical AI deployment, including explainability, fairness, and human-in-the-loop review processes 
Demonstrated ability to balance model performance and operational cost through dynamic inference strategies and model compression 
Experience right-sizing models, instance counts, and hardware types given requirements (e.g., context length, token inputs, token outputs)

rows.title: Plant Manager
rows.description:
The Plant Manager manages, directs and coordinates overall plant operations. Through subordinates, supervisors and managers, safety, continuous improvement, quality, cost, customer service, and production objectives are met or exceeded. Provides coaching and leadership to team members in the areas of safety, continuous improvement, productivity, quality, cost, equipment reliability, and employee engagement. Success relies on the ability to build relationships and fully engage all employees in business improvement.
Performance will be managed by the following critical metrics: lower conversion cost year over year, asset reliability, successful retention of key certifications in food safety, quality and organics, reduced total recordable injury rates, improved yields, employee retention and turnover, case fill rate and on time delivery.
The Plant Manager is responsible for the Manufacturing Operating Budget. This position directly and indirectly manages employees. The plant employs non-union and union full-time employees and salaried personnel.

Full time 
Location: 
MO St Louis 
Job Type: 
Production Operations

Plant Manager

​ Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k) with match, STD/LTD/AD&D/Life, HSA, FSA, EAP, Hospital indemnity, Accident Insurance, Identity and Fraud Protection Plan, Legal, and Critical Illness.​

Ensure adherence to all health and safety policies/protocols and promote a safety culture.
Lead the development, execution and monitoring of the operations strategy in line with the overall operational objectives to achieve performance, quality, and safety improvement and ensure achievement of manufacturing goals.
Assist in the development of operational and capital budgets, policies and procedures, and the execution of same.
Utilize available data including Operational Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), line speed target, and efficiency and process data to continuously improve productivity, uptime and reliability.
Continually coach, direct and train employees utilizing Lean principles. Monitor employees' work performance and attitude and perform formal reviews as required by policy.  Coach and counsel employees about work-related issues and assist employees to correct job skill deficiencies.

Lead the continuous improvement program to deliver opportunities in cost, quality, food safety and service.
Coordinates manufacturing activities with all other functions of the organization and suppliers to obtain optimum production and utilization of human resources, machines and equipment.

rows.description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.
Position Summary: 
At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work.  We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.
As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.
3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to: 
Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient
Required Qualifications: 
Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required
Essential Functions: 
Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
Attention and Focus: Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
Customer Service and Team Orientation: Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
Communication Skills: Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
Mathematical Reasoning: Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
Problem Resolution: Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options

Lift, scan, and bag items
Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions

Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs

Prepare independent cost estimates for submitted change order proposals
Analyze specifications, sketches, drawings, contract document agreements, and prior change order proposals
Become a subject matter expert on the contract verbiage for the contract being supported
Utilize knowledge of construction and estimating principles, theories, concepts, and industry practices and standards to perform moderately complex assignments under general supervision to produce accurate and quality cost estimates

The Team Leader is responsible for the complete operations of the store while on duty and acting as the Person in Charge unless a more senior level manager is present. Pritchard Industries is a dynamic and innovative provider of comprehensive facility services, dedicated to enhancing the operational efficiency of our client partners in the industries we serve. With services from facility maintenance and janitorial to landscaping and snow removal, we enable desired outcomes for our clients through consistent service and outstanding people. 
We are seeking an initiative-taking and experienced Chief Engineer to join our team.
The Chief Engineer will serve as Pritchard's on-site point of contact and function as liaison with the client Facilities Management Team. Chief Engineer will have complete authority to act on behalf of Pritchard. Perform engineering and mechanical services required for the safe and efficient operation of the building equipment and systems in a manner conducive to management's operating objectives. · Provide daily, weekly, and monthly reports to Management on the activities of the Engineering Department

· Promote programs for orientation and on-the-job safety training for new employees and sub- contracted staff.

rows.title: Benefits Manager
rows.description:
Union Square Hospitality Group (USHG) has created some of New York's most beloved restaurants, cafes, and bars, which offer outstanding food delivered with our signature warmth and hospitality. Founded by Danny Meyer with the opening of Union Square Cafe in 1985, the company now extends beyond the walls of its eateries. 
USHG has long supported its communities through hunger relief and civic organizations. USHG holds 28 James Beard Awards and numerous accolades for its distinctive style of hospitality. 
Who you are: 
At USHG, we start with each other. The Benefits Manager is responsible for overseeing Union Square Hospitality Group's employee benefits program. They will work with the People team and will play a critical role in ensuring that employees receive a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. This individual must be knowledgeable about benefits trends and regulations and have strong analytical, communication, and management skills.
What you'll do: 
Cultivate a culture of Enlightened Hospitality for all stakeholders that supports our business objectives and growth
Develop and implement employee benefits programs: The Benefits Manager researches, designs, and implements employee benefits programs. This includes health insurance, retirement plans, and other employee perks, such as wellness programs.
Communicate benefits information: The Benefits Manager communicates benefits information to USHG employees, including plan details, enrollment deadlines, and changes to the program. They may also provide training to employees on how to use the benefits program.
Monitor benefits trends: The Benefits Manager stays current on changes in laws and regulations related to employee benefits. They also monitor industry trends and make recommendations to improve the benefits program.
Manage vendor relationships: The Benefits Manager works with insurance providers, retirement plan administrators, and other vendors to negotiate contracts and ensure that services are delivered efficiently.
Analyze benefits data: The Benefits Manager analyzes benefits data to assess the effectiveness of the program and identify areas for improvement. They may also conduct surveys to gather feedback from employees about the benefits program.
Ensure compliance: The Benefits Manager ensures that the benefits program is compliant with all relevant laws and regulations, including the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA).
Collaborate with other teams: The Benefits Manager works with other teams, such as People, payroll, and finance, to ensure that the benefits program is integrated with other systems and processes.
Manage budget: The Benefits Manager manages the budget for the benefits program, including forecasting costs, monitoring expenses, and making recommendations for cost-saving measures. Communicates, promotes, and continues to evaluate our internal transfer/promotion process to support both business needs and employee growth needs
Vendor Relationships: The Benefits Manager will work and collaborate with the following vendors: BRI, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Fidelity, Cigna, Davis Vision, Wagmo, Unum, EB Cohen 
What we need from you: 
3-5 years of experience managing benefits preferably in the hospitality industry
Proficient in HR systems and extensive knowledge of benefits packages, policies, and legislation
Must be able to communicate effectively with senior leaders, build trust, credibility, and influence by example
Must have strong written, and verbal presentation and negotiation skills.
Sound HR judgment and sense of urgency
Keen understanding of the hospitality industry and the culture and beliefs of Union Square Hospitality Group
Knowledge of compensation and wage guidelines a plus
Bachelor's degree or relevant work experience required. SHRM Certification and UKG experience are a plus
What you'll get from us: 
At Union Square Hospitality Group,  extending Enlightened Hospitality is at the heart of everything we do. We believe our people are our greatest ingredient. Joining our team means becoming part of a culture rooted in care, creativity, and growth. As a Benefits Manager, you'll enjoy: 
Competitive pay and bonus potential : Annual compensation of $75,000 - $85,000 plus eligibility for a performance-based bonus, with consideration for your experience and impact 
Comprehensive health coverage :  Medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus flexible spending options for healthcare and dependent care 
Time to recharge: Generous paid time off and paid parental leave to support life outside of work 
Investing in your future: A matched 401(k) plan to help you grow long-term savings 
Peace of mind : Life insurance, employee assistance programs, and exclusive access to primary care, mental health, and other wellness services. 
Support in times of need: Access to the USHG HUGS Employee Relief Fund, offering direct assistance to team members facing unexpected hardship 
Dining Credit: An annual dining credit to enjoy exceptional meals and experiences at any of our restaurants  
Dining Discount: A 51% dining discount across the entire USHG family of restaurants to share unforgettable meals with friends and loved ones  
Convenience & flexibility: Pre-tax commuter benefits for transit and parking 
Growth and community: Opportunities for learning, mentorship, and collaboration with some of the most passionate people in hospitality. 
Putting Enlightened Hospitality into Practice 
Integral to our culture are our six behaviors. Our behaviors guide how we work together.
We play to win with humble swagger. Hospitality is a team sport where everyone deserves an opportunity to thrive and belong
Turn over the rocks and always be connecting dots to build uplifting experiences and relationships
Center the salt shaker with an unwavering commitment to excellence and the values that matter most
Write a great next chapter. The road to success is paved with mistakes well-handled
Bring a charitable assumption and err on the side of generosity
Leave our campsite better than we found it; always responsible for the impact of our wake

The responsibilities outlined above are not exhaustive. This role may be required to take on other duties or projects as necessary to support organizational goals, in alignment with their skills, experience, and the evolving needs of the business.

We Are: 
The Advanced Technology Centers (ATCs) is the engine for reinvention in our clients' transformation journey. Powered by more than 255,000 people across 24 countries, ATCs will provide our clients seamless access to industry insights and innovative technology solutions. 
Stronger together! 
The Advanced Technology Centers (ATCs) make tremendous impact in solving in our clients' business problems leveraging innovation, intelligence, industry insights, new IT and new technology skills. For our clients, the Network provides the strength of our geographic diversity, greater resilience, and seamless access to the deepest industry knowledge, the latest in Gen AI solutions, and tech expertise from around the world.

You Are: 
A transformation maven with the skills to help clients meet the challenges of digitization. Your superpower? Using your know-how to solve clients' most complex business problems to help their companies do more. You're as comfortable working in teams and leading projects as you are diving into the details of workstreams and configuring SAP solutions. And you work effectively with distributed onshore and offshore teams across time zones. 
The Work: 
As a SAP Ariba Lead, you will own the end-to-end design and delivery of Source to Pay on SAP Ariba, spanning Sourcing, Contract Management, Supplier Lifecycle and Performance, Requisitioning, Purchasing, Receiving, Invoicing, Tax determination and S/4HANA integration. You will lead client workshops, translate business requirements into configuration solutions, and run workstream activities with on- and off-shore resources. You are expected to be a subject matter expert, collaborate and manage the team to perform effectively, take responsibility for team decisions, engage with multiple teams, and provide solutions to problems within your immediate team and across multiple teams. Expert proficiency in SAP Ariba is required. Expert proficiency in SAP S/4HANA Materials Management and Cloud Integration Gateway is suggested. 
Use your business smarts to kick-start transformation programs, whether domain- or platform-led.
Independently deliver client workshops across the full Source to Pay lifecyle.
Design sourcing and contracting processes: source request creation, sourcing event and template design, contract negotiation and authorization, clause library setup, supplier onboarding, qualification and performance management.
Design procurement and payables processes: requisitioning, catalog and non-catalog buying, purchase order management, goods receipt, invoicing exception handling and tax determination.
Configure Ariba sourcing, contract management, buying & invoicing, Catalog Management and Commerce Automation to meet business requirements.
Define and configure approval workflows and parameter setup across the full process scope, including ICM parameters and Ariba Network rules.
Drive integration between SAP Ariba, S/4HANA Materials Management and downstream FI and PS modules using Cloud Integration Gateway.
Own data migration scope: master data, accounting data, cross application data, open contracts, and open purchase orders.
Lead template design for global deployment and rollouts, and identify process optimization and improvement opportunities. 
Produce Functional Design Documents and Technical Design Documents, and review deliverables produced by the team. 
Support testing across SIT, UAT and cutover, and resolve defects through hypercare.
Show clients how they can use SAP to solve their business problems.
Work in a team where you wear lots of hats: interacting with clients, managing workstreams, collaborating with other teams, and where you need to be in charge.
Interact with all workstreams: technical, reports, conversion, change management, project management, and more.
Tweak methods, tools, and procedures to create solutions that meet clients' needs.
Keep a record of requirements, solutions and impacts, alternatives and final decisions.
This role requires to be onsite 3 days per week. Preferred location: Montreal, Canada.

Minimum of 4years of experience in SAP Ariba, including depth in at least one of the following and working knowledge of the other: Ariba Strategic Sourcing Suite: Sourcing, Contract Management, Supplier Lifecycle and Performance
Ariba Procure to Pay and S/4HANA Materials Management
Minimum 4 years of SAP transformation, technical advisory or consulting experience, or 8 years of equivalent industry experience.
Minimum 3 years of experience across all project phases: Plan, Analyze, Design, Build, Test, Deploy and Support.
Minimum 1 year of experience as a Project, Large Workstream, or Client Lead on a large SAP transformational project with on- and off-shore resources.
A Bachelor's Degree
English is required for this position as this role will regularly interact with stakeholders across Canada, US and other countries across our Global footprint where English is the common language. Due to the significant high volume of interactions with these English-speaking stakeholders, which is inherent to this position, it is not possible to reorganize the company's activities to avoid this requirement.

You've obtained certification such as SAP Ariba Sourcing, SAP Ariba Contract Management, SAP Ariba Supplier Management, SAP Ariba Procurement, SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway, SAP Ariba Catalog Management, SAP S/4HANA Materials Management, SAP S/4HANA Sourcing & Procurement.
You've delivered SAP Ariba in a RISE with SAP or S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition landscape.

rows.title: Senior Associate,  Business Lending
rows.description:
BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $155 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.



We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/culture and learn more about how we work https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/careers.



About the team:

At Wealthsimple, we aren't just managing portfolios; we're rewriting the rules of how Canadians interact with credit. The Credit Analytics team own’s Wealthsimple's lending ecosystem, operating at the intersection of high-growth tech and data-driven underwriting.



We believe that being “credit-worthy” should mean more than just a traditional score. Our mission is to challenge the status quo, building inclusive products that empower millions of Canadians and the businesses they run to lead better financial lives. We’re growing fast, moving from small data to massive scale through iteration and experimentation.



We are extending our consumer credit expertise into business lending built for Canadian small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). This is a true green-field build — new adjudication policy, new underwriting signals, and new risk infrastructure, informed by everything we've learned scaling our consumer card portfolio.



About the role:

We are looking for a Senior Associate to own credit policy for our business lending products, starting with a business credit card — from adjudication through the full account lifecycle. You will design and implement the underwriting framework that determines who qualifies and at what limit, build the line management strategies that govern how those limits evolve, and partner closely with collections to manage risk once accounts are on book.



Small business cards can be underwritten on the owner, or on the business as it grows. You’ll be working with cash flow, seasonality, industry, and business bureau data, which is usually thinner and messier than consumer bureau data. We need someone who has worked across that range and can turn it into automated policy instead of file-by-file decisions.



You will collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, Data Science, Fraud, and Client Experience to translate policy into shippable adjudication and monitoring systems, and you will have significant ownership over how this portfolio’s risk appetite is defined from day one.



In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

 - Build a new lending program from the ground up with the breadth to see every part of it, from policy to funding, and the runway to grow into leading a lending line of business.

 - Design and own the adjudication policy for a new business credit card, including entity-level underwriting criteria, principal/guarantor assessment, joint-liability, initial limit-setting, and approval decisioning.

 - Own line management strategy for business credit products: credit limit increases and decreases, pricing, authorization rules, and active exposure management driven by cash-flow and balance monitoring.

 - Partner with the collections team to design risk-managed treatment strategies specific to business accounts, and to build lifecycle monitoring that catches emerging risk early.

 - Evaluate the performance of the business lending portfolio and your policies, using vintage analysis, cohort tracking, and champion/challenger testing to validate and refine underwriting decisions.

 - Propose policy enhancements that improve marginal profitability while keeping risk within appetite, informed by rigorous root-cause analysis rather than surface-level metrics.

 - Help define the data and underwriting infrastructure needed for SMB lending — including how to source, validate, and weigh business financial data alongside traditional bureau signals.

 - Influence roadmaps across partner teams (Engineering, Product, Data Science, Fraud, and Client Experience) and implement policy that drives measurable impact.

We're looking for someone who:

 - Has direct experience underwriting or setting credit policy for small and medium-sized businesses, this is a must-have for this role. Card experience isn't required; we'd love to hear from you if your background is in instalment loans or lines of credit.

 - Writes SQL hands-on to self-serve data and build monitoring and analytics.

 - Brings credit discipline to a ship-and-iterate environment, and is comfortable shaping policy while the product itself is still being defined.

 - Can turn analysis into a clear recommendation for technical and non-technical audiences, weigh incomplete or noisy information and still reach well-grounded decisions.

 - Is intellectually curious, passionate about their work, and wants ownership over their projects.

Preferred qualifications:

 - 5+ years of experience in small business lending

 - Knowledge of Canadian consumer credit bureau data (Equifax, TransUnion)

 - Working knowledge of how business credit risk differs from consumer credit risk: entity vs. personal guarantor assessment, business bureau data (e.g., business credit bureaus), cash-flow-based underwriting, industry/sector risk, and revenue seasonality.

 - Experience across the credit lifecycle: adjudication policy, line management, pricing, and collections strategy.

 - Experience with statistical/quantitative analysis: experimental design, champion/challenger (or A/B) testing, model accuracy validation, constrained optimization, decision trees, discounted cash flows, financial modeling.

 - Experience with Python, and GitHub. Airflow, AWS Redshift, and dbt are a plus.




WHY WEALTHSIMPLE?

🌸 Top-tier health benefits and life insurance

📈 Long-term group savings with employer match, through Wealthsimple for Business

🌴 20 vacation days, 4 wellness days, and unlimited sick and mental health days per year*

*Unlimited paid sick days, Wellness Days and the 90 day away program do not apply to certain roles.

That means we're always looking for better ways to work — whether that's new tools, AI, or rethinking how we approach a problem. We don't expect you to have all the answers, but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to evolve alongside the products we're building.

About the program: 
The Senior Living Management internship will be a full-time (40 hours/week) opportunity for 12 weeks from May to August. The Senior Living Management Intern is responsible for assisting the Executive Director and Administrator in the overall administration of the community. S/he also handles special projects for the Executive Director and Senior Leadership team members at the community. 
As part of the internship program, students will gain additional skills to prepare them for entering the job market, including interviewing, presentations, and performance evaluation to further enhance their experience. 
Experience is Everything; 
At LCS, experience is everything. We provide you the opportunity to use your talents in a progressive, growing organization that makes a positive difference in the lives of the seniors we serve. If you are seeking an organization that gives back, you’ll love working here. Our principles and hospitality promises define our company culture. LCS employees can be found participating in volunteer activities, getting involved in our committees or collaborating with team members in our innovative workspace. You’ll find several opportunities to grow as a professional, serve the community, and enhance the lives of the seniors. 
What You’ll Do: 
Attend and participate in department head meetings, care plan meetings, daily health center “stand up” meetings, board meetings, and other resident meetings as requested by the Executive Director. 
Make weekly environmental rounds (plant, kitchen, environmental services). 
Assist Administrator in preparing for yearly fire-safety and resident care survey inspections in the Health Center and Assisted Living areas. 
Conduct audits on a variety of Health Center documentation, including resident charts, MARs, TARs, pain assessments, etc. 
Attend interviews, counseling sessions, trainings and other personnel meetings. 
Attend marketing events as requested by the Executive Director. 
Prepare monthly financial variance reports for the Executive Director. 
Complete a variety of projects as prescribed by the Executive Director. 
What we’re looking for: 
Minimum of 1-2 years completed towards bachelor’s degree preferred. 
Currently enrolled in a college or university program majoring in Healthcare Management, Business, Nursing, Geriatrics, or related program. 
Interest in Senior Living operations is ideal 
Exposure to hospitality, or related field is a plus. 
Why join us? 
Hands-on experience in a professional environment 
Mentorship and exposure to senior leadership 
Opportunities for networking and career development 
Meaningful project work that makes an impact 
Competitive hourly rate: $22.50/hour 
Our Commitment 
LCS creates living experiences that enhance the lives of seniors. You’ll see this commitment in our people. They’re talented, dedicated professionals who truly care about residents, with each conducting his or her work with integrity, honesty and transparency according to the principles of LCS. We strive to help every community succeed—strengthening available resources, establishing proven practices that lead to long-term growth and value for those living in, working for and affiliated with the community. Check us out on our website: https://www.lcsliving.com
